messages.author: b2d9d2614971143c
messages.subject: LOO for brmsfit objects
parts:
I noticed in the rstanarm implementation of loo, they have a nice feature where: "If k_threshold is not NULL and there are J observations with k estimates above k_threshold then when loo is called it will refit the original model J times, each time leaving out one of the J problematic observations. The pointwise contributions of these observations to the total ELPD are then computed directly and substituted for the previous estimates from these J observations that are stored in the object created by loo"

Based on the brms documentation it doesn't seem like the LOO function takes this approach when used on brmsfit objects (correct me if I'm wrong). Is this a feature that can be added? Or is there an existing way to take this approach when very few data points have k>0.7?

Many thanks,

Christina

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: LOO for brmsfit objects
parts:
You are right, this is not yet possible in brms, but it sounds like a useful feature.

Would you mind opening an issue on github (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms), so that I don't loose track of it?

Best,
Paul
